column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
Kept the Musical Herald quotation as paraphrase. 'The Ants Go Marching' named in wp as 'Ants Go Marching'.
wp says he held Guelders 1538-1543; entry says he ruled the United Duchies from 1539: no conflict, kept both as given.
The entry's 'John III' is the same John, bishop of Liège, the article names as William's brother; I wrote 'her uncle John, the bishop of Liège' without the numeral.

Article says nothing of the 1830 revolution, the constitution or the co-regency; not touched. Tatiana's descent is through the Fabrice line per the list; wp also says through her mother's side. Kept general.
Article title is 'William of Villehardouin'; entry uses 'William II'. Avoided repeating the Pelagonia capture and ceded forts already in the entry.
Conflict: entry says the second term ran from 1729; article says George II reappointed him on 22 October 1728 and gives the term as 1728-1732. Left the year out.

The article's account of his early career is muddled (the wife 'from Wei', Wey/Wei confusion); kept only in general terms. Article says he was 'executed' in 381; entry says nobles killed him beside the king's corpse: wrote only that his life ended in 381 BCE. Article gives 440 without c.; entry has c. 440: no date printed.
Kept to dated, lasting facts; recognition disputes of Texas groups left out.
The article says he convinced Genghis Khan to spare Kaifeng, but Kaifeng's siege fell after Genghis's death; wrote 'the Mongols' without naming the khan.

The article contradicts itself on Huguang: promoted viceroy of Huguang in August 1889 (as the entry says), and elsewhere 'in 1896 ... moved to Wuchang to serve as the Viceroy of Huguang'. No date for Wuchang printed.
'handbook of diction' rendered as 'handbook of rhetoric'.

Article lead says Parliament prohibited such insurance in 1791, while the abolition section says the 1794 renewal of the 1788 Act limited the insurance policies; I used the 1794 version only, consider checking.
Short article; about 270 words. Monorail project left out (status 'as of 2021').
Article contradicts itself on the Grand Council (lead: appointed 1884; biography: 1880) and on Shaan-Gan (1866 in the lead, 1867 in the biography): no dates printed for these.

Article calls A'ali a major town in northern Bahrain (Northern Governorate) and also says it is in the middle of the island; entry calls it a village in central Bahrain. Used the island's middle and the governorate only. Article gives no 2050-1750 BCE dating; entry's dates not repeated. Names in the inscription written without the transliteration marks.
The article says sources give 715, 716 or 718 for his death; the entry says 716. No year printed. The article gives no date for the treaty with Theodemir (entry: 713).
Short article; about 270 words. The 1942 incident is not in the article.
The entry dates him 1080–1169; the article gives c. 1080 – 1170 in the lead and says he lived in Damascus from 1169 until his death. The year of death is left out of the text.
The article gives his death as 20 March 1286 in the lead and 21 March 1286 in the body; the text gives only March 1286.

The entry says Louis the Pious exiled him in 814 and restored him in 821; the article ties the exile to Bernard of Italy's bid of 817 and says he was recalled after seven years. Both the year of exile and of recall are left out. The article gives his death as 2 January 827 in the lead and 1 January 827 in the body; the text says early in January 827. The article spells the work De ordine palatinii (usually De ordine palatii); kept as the article has it.
The article says the request to Ethiopia has been denied 'to date'; the text states only that it was made.
The article says they were driven out of Norway in 1034 or 1035; the entry says 1035. No year given in the text.

The article dates the start of their rule to about 550 and lists Garibald I as duke 548–591; the entry says about 555. Neither year is given. The article also doubts Garibald's membership in the family, which is told as modern scholarship's view.
The article says he completed Mem and Zin at the age of 44 (born 1650, so about 1694); the entry says it was completed in 1692. The date of completion is left out of the text.
The article's lead gives the migration from Tado to southern Benin as 12th or 13th century; consistent with the entry. The 1724 conquest of Allada and the 8,000 captives are as the article states.
The entry dates him 842–891; the article gives his birth as 29 November 843. The birth date is left out of the text.
The article's list of works dates the dissertation 1917 while the text gives the PhD as 1918 (as the entry does); no year is given for the dissertation in the text.
The entry's seven-year confinement of Tasso is not in the article, which only names Alfonso as Tasso's patron.

The entry calls him of Georgian origin; the article gives both Abkhaz and Georgian versions of his origin. The text names only his birthplace, Abkhazia, and does not discuss his ethnic origin. The entry says he died of wounds; the article says he was killed in Cairo. The text says only that he died in Cairo in 1773. The article says he lost power in 1772 but notes that date is disputed (1769 in al-Jabarti and the Sicill-i Osmani, 1773 in Uzuncarsili); no year given.

The article says he joined the Bolshevik Party in 1920; left out as doubtful and unexplained. The article calls the 1917 party the Alash Autonomy in one place and the Alash party in the lead; the text uses Alash party for the party.
Left out: the 2025 film and the lithium find announced in 2025 (estimates, not lasting facts), and transport details.
The article gives the signing as 26 August 1936 in the lead and 27 August in the section on the signing; the text says August 1936.

The article dates MacCarthy's translation 1893 in one place and 1895 in the list of editions; no year given. The entry says compiled in the late fifteenth century from older collections, consistent with the article.
The article calls the enemy alliance the Northwestern Confederacy; the entry says Western Confederacy. The text names no confederacy.
The article says most victims were rehabilitated 'after 1959' in the lead but describes rehabilitation after Mao's death in 1976; the text follows the latter.
Article: terms 1870-1877, 1879-1884, 1886-1887; the entry's 'dominated from 1870 to 1888' is not contradicted, so the end year of the third term is left vague ('again from 1886').
Entry says the October 2016 attacks were on police posts; article says military/border posts along the border. Worded as 'posts along the Bangladesh-Myanmar border'.
SKIPPED: article has about 300 words, nearly all already in the entry's description
The article gives no year for the war against Antipas; the entry's 36 CE is left unrepeated.
Entry says excavations since the 1930s; article: minor digs in 1890, large-scale from 1943 to 1948 under Andria Apakidze, resumed 1985. No excavation dates given in the text.
Article dates his return to Spain to 1872 yet ties it to Pavia's coup (January 1874): no year given. Article's 'Two years later at age 53' for the second Cuban posting is confused: left undated.
Entry dates 1338-1378; article gives birth 23 January 1340 (and 'born in 1340'). Birth year left out of the text.

Article's dates conflict: lead 18 February 1547 - 1 September 1621; wall ceramics 27 February 1547 / 30 August 1621; gravestone March 1546 / August 1622. Entry 1547-1621; no exact dates given in the text. Article both says he was 'principal planner' of Isfahan and that no design can be substantiated; text keeps both as credited and unsubstantiated.

Entry says Philip rebuilt the city around 2 BCE; article says he founded it in 3 BCE. Year left out (Philip not dated in the text). Article says Herod's temple to Augustus may be at nearby Omrit; left out.

Article gives the Cyprus campaign as 1424-26 without the capture date; the entry's 1426 is not restated. Article says Barsbay married Shahzada 'in 1537', an evident slip; left out. Alanya not in the article.
Article's French strength is given inconsistently ('three-to-one', 'twice as many', Digby Smith's 40,000 infantry); no ratio given in the text.

Article's lead dates the battle 4 July 1610, while it has Żółkiewski moving on 3 July and the Warsaw tomb inscription reads 2 VII. No day given in the text. Other loss estimates in the article: 5,000 for Shuisky's army and 400 for the Poles; Swedish losses 200-2,000.
Article does not mention the occupation of Jutland named in the entry; not repeated.

Entry says the stand kept 'the road open to join with the Prussians'; the article calls the battle a strategic French success because Wellington could not aid Blücher at Ligny, while crediting it with letting him reach Waterloo. Text states both facts without a verdict.
Article gives 23 January 1565 but says the precise date is debated; the entry says January 1565, so no day is given. The later capital is spelt Pengonda as in the article.
Article dates veneration from the 13th century; the canonisation year 1523 is in the entry already.
The entry spells the battle Ellendun; the article Ellandun. Used the article's form with its modern location.
Article names the father Ernst I, Duke of Saxe-Coburg-Altenburg, while the entry calls him Ernest the Pious of Saxe-Gotha; the father's title is left out.

The article does not date the kingdoms beyond oral traditions from the 17th century, nor give Merina as the conqueror (it names Radama I); the entry's 18th-century kingdoms and Merina conquest are not contradicted.

The article both says the lighthouse was built during the Dutch settlement and by the British, and both that ships came until 1958 and that the port was closed under British rule; who built the lighthouse and when the port closed are left out.
The entry speaks of the rise and fall of Mayapan; the article does not mention Mayapan, so it is not repeated.

The entry dates the Viking occupation of Repton 873–874; the article gives 874 for the march to Repton. Only 874 for his expulsion is given, which both share. The article is short; the text runs to about 260 words.
The 2000 Arusha Agreement is in the entry already and is not retold; the article says the government and Tutsi groups signed it in August 2000 while two main Hutu rebel groups refused.
Recent council disputes (2013-2014) and the names of present office-holders left out as present-day politics of a living people; the article's list is 'as of 2025'.
The article gives 1 July 1948 as the date he was elected; the entry says only 1948.

The article's sentence on the Franco-Prussian War ('participated only in "Samaritan"') is garbled; rendered as relief work for the wounded. Left out the unclear clause about Schleswig in 1849 and the claim the Andersen relationship was romantic (Andersen's own account).

The article dates the first Marinid burial and small mosque to 1284–85 (Umm al-'Izz, wife of Abu Yusuf Ya'qub), while the entry places the building of the burial ground in the 14th century; I left out the start date. The entry calls Sala Phoenician; the article says a Phoenician settlement is debated, so the text hedges.
The article dates the culture to the 2nd to 5th centuries AD; the entry says 3rd and 4th centuries. I gave no span. The article says its end came in the 5th century; I left the century out.
The article gives no date for the end of the domain; the entry's 1871 is not repeated. The article's ichinomiya detail (Sumiyoshi or Hakozaki Shrine) left out.

The article's lead dates the war 1865 to 1879 (to the peace treaties), the entry 1864–1866; no span given in the text. The treaty dates (Peru 1879, Bolivia 1879, Chile 1883, Ecuador 1885) agree with the entry's 1870s and 1880s but were left out as the entry covers them. Spain as 'fourth largest naval power' left out (ranking).
Thin article (about 350 words); two sections only. The article does not name the Ma'n dynasty; I left the dynasties to the entry. The 1989 Israeli air strike left out as a minor incident.

The article dates Antigonus's victory near Corinth, in which Areus I was killed, to 265 BCE; the entry gives no year, so I left the year out. Thin article (about 340 words): the text stays near the minimum.
The article says John Louis II died 'only four years later' than 1742, i.e. about 1746, consistent with the entry's 'shortly before his death in 1747'; I gave no year for it.
The article says he was trained 'from 1570', when he was two; date left out.
The entry calls Fleurus no defeat but lists Höchst and Stadtlohn; the text tells Fleurus as the article does (claimed by both sides).

The entry says the council gave way to the Constituent Assembly in 1920; the article says the Assembly first met on 15 May 1920 but that the council was not replaced by a parliament until 2 August 1922. I told neither ending.

The article gives several conflicting surrender figures (about 135,000 by 12 May; about 180,000 from the Baltic area; 146,000 by Russian records; about 190,000 by current scholarship) and names both Govorov and Bagramyan as accepting the surrender. I left the figures and the name out. It also dates the pocket to 22 May 1945, the entry to May 1945.

The article contradicts itself on Ariminum: its lead has Caesar occupying Ariminum and then crossing, its body has his legate Hortensius taking the town before Caesar crossed. I followed the body without saying who crossed first. The dinner with Sallust and others left out.
The article names both Tarquinius Superbus and Tarquinius Priscus as the king of the Sibylline Books story; the entry says King Tarquin, which I kept.

The article mixes the Nangnang (Lelang) Commandery and a Nakrang Kingdom; I kept its wording and dates. It does not say whether Daemusin died in 44; the entry's reign ends in 44, and the text gives no death.
Kept the coup's date and place to the entry. The quoted quips are reported ('is reported to have said'); left out.
Thin article (about 400 words); two sections. The article calls the revived 1765 body Det Guineiske kompagni and dates its end 1776, which fits the entry's 1754–1776.

SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance, most of it already in the entry; it also dates his death 1085 (Michael the Syrian) against the entry's 1084, and cites Maalouf for his fighting the First Crusade in 1097

The article names the 60th emir both Faruk Umar Faruk and Umar Faruk Umar, and dates Malam Musa's installation both 1904 and 1903–04; I gave neither. Its 'Daure-Zango' and 'Daure-Baure' simplified to Zango and Baure.

The article gives the cousins' joint rule as 1246–1256 in its lead and 1247/1248–1259 in the body; I gave no span. It also says David VI was crowned at Kutaisi as joint sovereign by his mother in 1230, while the entry says crowned as co-ruler with his cousin; I left out the 1230 coronation. Article's 'Batu Khan in Karakorum' left vague as 'the Mongols'.

The article dates the Abbasi renovation to 1732; the entry says the nawabs took and rebuilt the fort in 1733. Left the year out. The article says the nawabs took the fort from the Shahotra tribe, lost it in 1747 and retook it in 1804, and that the British later used it as a prison; the entry says it was held by Bhati Rajputs before the nawabs and remained with the nawabs' family. Left these points out.
SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance; almost nothing is known of his life
The article gives both 1325 (attribution to Mansa Musa) and 1327 (built); the entry says the 1320s. Left the exact year out.
Left out the Gini index, poverty headcount and the 2025 Politburo resolution (present-day figures and policy).

The article's lead dates the chariot burials c. 2000 BCE and the chariot to around 2000 BCE; the entry gives Sintashta and Petrovka as about 2100–1700 BCE, which the article also gives. Avoided a single date.
The article gives Magellan's death as 27 April 1521; not in the entry, left out as the entry gives no date for Mactan.
The article says he was confirmed as hegemon at Jiantu 'the next year' after Chengpu (632 BCE); the entry implies 632 BCE. Left the year out.
The article speaks once of 'nearly a million Dzungars' slain while also giving Wei Yuan's pre-war population of 600,000; used only the attributed Wei Yuan figures.
Article is short (about 600 words) and says nothing on the buildings, the cone mosaics, the tablets or the Warka Vase named in the entry; the text covers the temple's administration and cult only.
Left out the article's partisan judgements of his tactics ('fatal flaw', 'failed miserably'), which are unattributed.
The article spells the king Senwosret II and the princess Sithathor-yunit; kept the entry's spellings (Senusret, Sithathoriunet not repeated).
SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance beyond a list of children; adds little to the description
Left out present membership figures, current commanders and equipment.
Article is on the Eteocretan language; it covers the people through the ancient testimony, which fits the entry.
The article's lead says Jews had to leave 'by the end of July'; its section on conditions says the period was extended to 10 August. Used 10 August from the decree section.
The article gives no year for the Toxcatl massacre, so none is printed.
The entry says Martí was arrested before the uprising broke out; the article does not give the timing of his arrest, so it is left out.

The entry dates Kodok as the royal centre from about the 16th century; the article says the kingdom was independent for more than sixteen centuries and Kodok was hidden for over 500 years. No period printed. The article's 1964 massacre is under 'the reign of Muhammad Ahmad Mahjub'; left unnamed.
The entry says he was on holiday in Switzerland; the article says he travelled abroad, likely to warn the West. Neither motive printed.
Left out the widow's 2025 accusations against the Attorney General and President Daniel Noboa (a present government).
The article says nothing of the Muscogee towns or the treaty cessions named in the entry; nothing on them is added.

The article dates construction 1624-1634 and says the permanent fort was built 'four years later' than the temporary one; no year for the permanent fort is printed. Third section is mostly the fort's design; the article says little about what survives today.
The article dates the memorandum May 1936; month not printed.
The article's lead says the Marathas fought against Mysore, its Background that they kept strategic neutrality; the text follows the Background.

The entry names the siege of Nice in 1543 as the best-known joint action; the article's text given here (a section opening only) peaks the alliance with Corsica in 1553 and does not describe Nice. Neither ranking printed; Corsica given as 'the high point of the military alliance' as the article's lead says.
The article says the female line continued after 1671 through Maria Juliana Frankopan; the text says only that the Trsat branch ended.

The article dates Napoleon's reinstatement 1806 in the lead and 1804 in the body, and the repeal 1789 and 1790; no year printed. It also says the gabelle lasted until 1946 and was abolished in 1945; the entry's 1945 is not contradicted. The article ascribes a '1640 codification of gabelle law' to Jean-Baptiste Colbert, which looks doubtful; neither name nor year printed.
The entry says he was probably deposed around 591; the article says it is unknown whether he was deposed or died. The text gives the article's uncertainty without contradicting 'probably'.
The article gives his death as 25 March 1913 in the lead and 26 March 1913 in the body; only the month is printed.
SKIPPED: The article has under 250 words of substance: birth, the 1567 division, two marriages, a list of children and his burial; nothing on his government.
The article says he was dismissed (lead) and retired citing health (body); the text gives the body's account.

The article's lead gives his Corsican viceroyalty as 1794-1796 (as the entry does) but its Career section says he was appointed in 1796; the appointment year is left out. The article's family section dates the wedding to 1777; the Westminster Abbey inscription quoted in the article gives Vienna 1779, contradicting 1799-1801; left out.
The article says Uzun Hasan died in January 1478, consistent with the entry.

The entry calls him legate of Romagna; the article says legate of Ravenna, so the text says 'legate at Ravenna' without contradicting. The article dates his appointment over the San Lazzaro hospital to 1730 while placing it after his retirement in 1740; the year is left out. The Political Testament of 1753, of questioned authenticity, left out.
The entry gives the date 26 August 2019 (the first posting on LIHKG); the text does not repeat it. The entry is written as a work; the article's claims about Ukraine's slogan left out as unclear.
Length given as 23.80 m in the article; the entry's 'about 23 metres' is not repeated.
The article romanises Yi Seong-gye as Yi Sŏnggye and Jeong Mong-ju as Chŏng Mong-ju; the article's spellings are used. Died 17 May 1394 per the article; the entry gives 1394.

The article's lead says the first lowland sections opened by 1875, its history section by 1874; written as 'the mid-1870s'. The entry's figure 'about fifteen kilometres' agrees with 15,003 m. Louis Favre and workers' deaths (in the entry) are not in the saved text.
The article writes both 'diarchy' and 'dyarchy'; 'diarchy' used. Bhulabhai Desai's speech and Amery's reply left out for length.
The entry dates the attack on the Obodrites and Reric to 808; the article does not give the year, so none is stated. The article's '200 sails' rendered as 200 ships.
SKIPPED: article has about 300 words, nearly all already in the entry
Census figures (1994: about 1.4 million, 2.7%) left out as dated statistics.
SKIPPED: article has about 300 words; little beyond the entry

The entry dates the present building mainly to the late 13th and 14th centuries; the article says no finds can be firmly dated before the 1320s and only 'generally considered' 13th century. The 1320s point is left out of the text. Short article (about 400 words); three sections kept brief.

The article's Thatcher paragraph dates the Convention of Peking to 1856 and the 1898 convention to 1890, against its own lead and treaty list (1860, 1898); the treaty list's dates are used. The article's lead says 'Hong Kong is now widely regarded as being under tight control'; left out as a judgement on present government. The article does not give the year of the British concession in November, so none is stated. The article also says 'the capture of Hong Kong Island in 1841' and 156 years of rule.
The article gives the date of death as 2 February 1512, consistent with the entry.
The article gives 7 or 10 September 1474 for the formal request; left out.
The article says he served as vice-president until 24 December 1990, when a coup overthrew the government.
The entry calls him viceroy of Kush; the saved article does not mention it, so the point is not repeated. Shoshenq I's accession dated 943 BC in the article.
The entry says he was killed in June 1869; the article gives 20 June 1869 (solar), lunar 11 May. Toba–Fushimi written with a hyphen.
The article: tried October 1947 to January 1948; the entry says sentenced in 1948. Consistent. The Soviet request for his execution left out.
The entry's Ryuzoji, Arima and Omura are not in the article; not used.

Article says the main line ruled the duchy until 1630 and that Anna von Croy, daughter of Bogislaw XIII and the last member of the house, died in 1660; the entry says the family died out with Bogislaw XIV in 1637. Both left out. Wartislaw I's death: lead says 1135, family tree 'between 1134 and 1148'; not used. Entry's conversion in the 1120s is not in the article.

Article says Hugh was not released after Fariskur until March 1252; the entry dates his part in Louis IX's crusade 1248-1250. Release date left out. Article gives death as '27 or 30 October' in the lead and 27 October in the Death section; used 27 October. Article says 'aged 60', though by his birth on 9 March 1213 he was 59; age left out.
Article dates the Byzantine tribute variously ('for 15 years' after 937; peace treaty after the 934 campaign); used 'after 934' as in the timeline.
SKIPPED: article under 250 words of substance; adds little beyond the description beyond census and climate figures
SKIPPED: article under 250 words of substance (one short life section and a list of children); note: article gives death c. 1201, entry 1202
Article gives birth as 29 November 1814; the entry's dates say 1815. Birth date left out.

Article dates the Kaga Rebellion to 1486 (and mentions '1488 rebellions' elsewhere); the entry says 1488. Year left out. Article gives the Ishiyama Hongan-ji siege as 11 years ending in 1580; the entry says Nobunaga was resisted for a decade. Length left out; surrender year 1580 also left out of the history to avoid repeating the description.
Article says Roman law was first taught at Bologna in the 1070s and that Irnerius founded his school in 1084 or 1088; kept the latter only.
The entry names the sculptor 'Nikolaus of Haguenau' and the place Isenheim; the article uses Nikolaus Hagenauer and Issenheim. Used the article's forms; the editor may harmonise.
Article dates Amenemhat I's reign c. 1991-1962 BC and the foundation to his year 20; the entry gives 'around 1980 BCE'. No date given in the text.

Article calls the life grant 'iqta'a' in the lead; not used. The entry says Mughal jagirs were usually transferable rather than hereditary; the article says jagirs became hereditary in practice. The hereditary point left out.
Entry's Later Baekje base is not in the article; not used. Population 'as of January 2024' omitted per guide.
Article gives death 3 March 264 and the revolt starting 'in March 264'; kept both as the article has them. Entry says he joined Zhuge Liang in 228: consistent.

Article places his enfeoffment with Qi after the Duke of Zhou's campaigns against the Dongyi that followed the Rebellion of the Three Guards; the entry says he was enfeoffed after Muye. Timing of the enfeoffment not stated in the text.

The article gives inconsistent population figures for around 1700 (lead: roughly 500 plantation owners and 9,000 enslaved; History: 570 citizens) and the Essai Historique's 1,000 in 1677; none printed. The article's lead says the settlement was established in the 1600s and a 1652 group under Lord Willoughby settled there; left out as unclear.
The article spells the lament 'Con lagrime bagnadome' and 'Con lagreme bagnandome el viso'; one spelling used. 'San Biagio' rendered from the article's 'St. Biagio di Roncalea'; checker may flag.
The article gives his marriage to Janice Clarke as 1968 in one section and 1967 in another; not printed.

The article gives his birth as about 1384 or more likely around 1387; the entry's c. 1387 kept by not printing a year. 'Struck by a cannonball' paraphrases 'enemy ordnance'; could be changed to 'struck by enemy fire' if too specific.
The article says Jolof was reduced to a kingdom and was effectively over by 1600; the entry says it 'broke apart after its coastal provinces rebelled', consistent.

The article says Calcutta was besieged by the French in 1748, which looks like a slip; left out. The article's lead gives his birth date as unknown while its body gives 23 January 1697 (matching the entry); the body's date used.
SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance and adds little beyond the description

The article spells 'Sancisi Weerdenburg' without hyphen; check-more may flag the hyphenated form. The article's lead and body describe the shape as rectangular with a square base; the entry's 'square stone tower' not contradicted.
The article gives his reign as c. 1375 to 1360 BC; the entry has c. 1374 to 1360 BCE, so no years printed. Ekur's 'House of the Mountain' and the diacritics of Egalmaḫ and Šamaš simplified.

The entry says the Kalbids completed the conquest of the island; the article gives Taormina's fall in 902, before the dynasty, and does not say they completed it. Neither version printed. The article gives al-Akhal's reign as 1017-1037 in the text and 1019-1037 in the ruler list; no years printed.

The article gives the naval battle as 11 August 1791 and as beginning on 31 July 1791 (two calendars); only the year printed. The voivode and the king are named as the article spells them ('Mircea Stari', 'Vladislav III').

The article gives his capture of Durrës as both 1367 and 1368 (the entry has 1368); no year printed for it. The article says Gjergj Thopia succeeded him; the entry says Durrës passed to Venice after his death. Not in direct conflict, both left as they stand. The article dates Balsha's offensive to 1385 and the capture to 'the following year'; worded as '1385 or 1386'. Could be reworded to 'in 1386' if the editor prefers.

The entry's patronage by the Rinpungpa and Tsangpa and the Gelug victory of 1642 are not in the article; nothing on them written. The article's lead says the 2nd among the 10 Karmapas advised Chinese emperors (garbled); left out.

The entry says he fled to the Byzantine Empire in 1261; the article says he lost Iconium on 12 August 1261 and fled to Constantinople in summer 1262 (and had earlier fled to Nicaea in 1257). The year of the flight to Constantinople is not printed. The article says he was sultan until 1262; not printed.
The article gives the opening to the public as 1871 in its lead and 7 May 1874 in its body (the entry has 1874); not printed. 'Sea of Japan' for the article's 'Japan Sea'; checker may flag.
The article gives the range's length as about 310 km (the entry has about 300); not printed. The article gives the highest peak, Zardak, as 2,260 m in the lead and 2,895 m in the body; not printed.
The article says that after Taiwan he 'spent the following decade' as Minister of the Army under Itō Hirobumi, which does not fit the entry's Taiwan tenure of 1898-1906; left out.
The article does not use the name Ufa Directory; the Provisional All-Russian Government is the same body. The article's dissolution sentence is ambiguous about what Kappel dissolved; worded loosely.
The article does not give the year of Kokand's annexation (the entry has 1876); no year printed for it.
Article lists 'World Heritage Site' loosely in one paragraph but the section says Tentative List only; used the Tentative List.
The entry says Portugal held the town until 1550; the article says John III decided to abandon it in 1533 and the final evacuation came in 1549. The year of departure is left out.
Article gives the cathedral as seat of the bishop since 1983 but the first bishop served from 1982; the year is left out.
Article says La Isabela was depopulated/abandoned by 1500; entry's end date is 1498. No end year given in the text.
Article chronology: city occupied 900-400 BCE; heads carved by 700 BCE, possibly 850 BCE. Consistent with entry.
Entry dates the raising to around 105 CE; article says Graham Webster assigns 101 and that the only firm date is existence by 108. No founding year given in the text.
Entry's statement that he sided with Prussia in 1866 is not in the article; not repeated.

SKIPPED: the article's history is three sentences (formed 1818 from Cambria, Étienne Brûlé 1615); the rest is present-day directory matter (officials, fire companies, census figures, school rankings, roads), and nothing on the Tuscarora settlement or the burning of 1813 that the entry names
The entry says she was a mistress of the Prince of Wales; the article says it was 'presumed'. Kept the article's wording without contradicting the entry.
Article: over 90% killed in the Holocaust; entry gives 90-95 per cent. No percentage repeated.
